_: MLP-split crossover, thorough tier: the per-candidate break-even table and
the envelope. Four arms, three concentration vectors.
Read the quick tier's file first -- the reasoning, the cache-bypass proof
and the pinned KV ownership vector are the same and are not repeated here.
WHAT THIS TIER ADDS. Three candidates instead of one, so the result is not
a single break-even but an envelope: which vector is the best choice at
which prompt:output mix, and which candidate is never the best choice at
any mix and is therefore not proposable at all. That last verdict is
structural and needs at least three candidates to be visible.
WHAT ONE INVOCATION COVERS. One point, all four arms interleaved. The
point below is the prefill half at 4000 prompt tokens. The full space:
phase=random-ids output_tokens=1   prompt_tokens=500
phase=random-ids output_tokens=1   prompt_tokens=1000
phase=random-ids output_tokens=1   prompt_tokens=2000
phase=random-ids output_tokens=1   prompt_tokens=4000   (this file)
phase=random-ids output_tokens=1   prompt_tokens=8000
phase=random-ids output_tokens=1   prompt_tokens=11000
phase=random     output_tokens=256 prompt_tokens=400
TIME. 3 noise-floor boots + 2 interleaved repeats over 4 arms = 11 boots
per point, 7 points = 77 boots. At ~3.5 min per boot that is ~270 min.
Run it overnight, or run the quick tier first and only come back here if
the quick tier found a crossover worth locating precisely.
STOPPING EARLY IS ALLOWED AND IS IN THE SCENARIO. The prefill gain is a
SLOPE difference and saturates as a percentage past roughly 2000 tokens.
Once two consecutive lengths give the same per-prompt-token slope inside
the prefill noise floor, the remaining lengths cost time and add nothing.
SPECULATION IS ON in the decode point of this tier, which is why the
decode metric is ms per SPECULATIVE STEP rather than ms per output token:
under speculation the per-token time fuses accept length with step time
and the two arms need not have the same accept length.
PATHS COME FROM THE ENVIRONMENT. model_path, the draft model and
python_exe are written as ${MODEL_ROOT:-<MODEL_ROOT>}/... and
${VENV:-<VENV>}/bin/python; load_study expands them. Source your local
rig env file before running. The defaults are placeholders on purpose --
an unsourced run fails on a visibly bogus path instead of booting
against whatever tree this file's author happened to have.
